properties.decision: Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal — Alex's idea (v0.47.0, 2026-09-05), in his words: 'Could auto assign next-in-sequence or say so in the error.' Two options he named: (a) AUTO-ASSIGN — `sequence` becomes optional and, when omitted, the tool writes max(existing)+1; one call, no scan. (b) NAME IT IN THE ERROR — `sequence` stays required, but the refusal says 'the highest existing sequence is N' so the second call can be right. WHAT IS CHEAP: (b) is a handler pre-check before the generic required-field helper, the same shape as the add_change_event description redirect (#429); no schema change, no semantics change. (a) is also cheap to code.
properties.name: OPEN — add_epoch requires `sequence` but the refusal cannot say what value would work. Should the tool auto-assign next-in-sequence, or should the refusal name the current maximum?
properties.rationale: THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (a), from the record: sequences are not just order — they are deliberately SPACED and re-ordered. chg:the-philosophy-epoch-makes-room-for-a-cut moved a planned epoch 360 -> 365 so a release cut could take the sequence at which it actually happened. An auto-assigned max+1 would pack every new epoch against the last one and leave no room for exactly that move, and it would silently choose a position the user may not mean (a planned epoch usually belongs AFTER a gap, not immediately next). So (a) trades a round-trip for a quiet positional claim — the defaults-do-not-assert concern in a new coat. (b) removes the scan without making a choice for anyone. A middle path: (b) now, and auto-assign only when the caller passes an explicit `sequence: "next"` — a stated request, not a default. A ranking is a finding, not a decision; Anthony rules.
